content_voiceover: This slide details post transplant maintenance therapy. Recommended options include thalidomide at fifty to one hundred milligrams daily, lenalidomide at ten to twenty five milligrams daily, though this isn't yet first line reimbursed, or the maximum dose an individual patient can tolerate. Proteasome inhibitors can also serve as maintenance, bortezomib for example can be given every two weeks at one point three milligrams per square meter. Based on clinical trial data, patients who received daratumumab as part of first line therapy may also continue it as maintenance, dosed roughly every one to two months, though this again lacks health insurance reimbursement currently. Maintenance is generally continued until disease progression or unacceptable drug related toxicity. It's worth noting the literature suggests long term lenalidomide maintenance may increase the risk of second primary malignancies, but international consensus still holds that the benefits outweigh the risks, so physicians should discuss this tradeoff with patients. For proteasome inhibitor based maintenance, two years of treatment can be considered. Timing wise, maintenance should begin within one to two months after autologous transplant or consolidation, ideally no later than three months. The NCCN table below reinforces lenalidomide as the preferred category one maintenance option, with carfilzomib plus lenalidomide or daratumumab plus lenalidomide as other recommended choices, and bortezomib, daratumumab alone, or ixazomib reserved for certain circumstances.
keypoints: Lenalidomide is preferred maintenance, thalidomide and bortezomib are alternatives
Daratumumab maintenance is an option after frontline use, not yet reimbursed
Continue maintenance until progression or intolerable toxicity
Long-term lenalidomide raises secondary malignancy risk but benefit outweighs risk
Start maintenance within 1 to 2 months post-transplant, no later than 3 months
keypoint_voiceover: Remember lenalidomide is the preferred maintenance agent per NCCN, with bortezomib, daratumumab, and ixazomib as alternatives in select patients. Watch for the secondary malignancy risk with long term lenalidomide, and start maintenance promptly, within one to two months of finishing transplant or consolidation.
